cards.title: Loan repayments followed by new advances (bed and breakfasting)
cards.question: Was a repayment of at least the s464C amount followed within 30 days by new advances of at least that amount?
cards.notes: The repayment is matched against the new advance and does not reduce the s455 charge to that extent. Repayments by dividend or bonus chargeable to income tax are excluded (s464C(4)).

cards.title: Repayments with arrangements to redraw
cards.question: Where the balance was at least the arrangement threshold, were there arrangements to redraw at the time of repayment?
factors: Balance before repayment at or above the arrangement threshold
New advances of at least the s464C amount after the repayment, at any interval
Evidence of intention or arrangements at the time of repayment
cards.reasoning: The pattern is consistent with arrangements to redraw. Prudently, the repayment is treated as matched until the reviewer records otherwise.

cards.title: Settlements legislation - income shifting through shares
cards.question: Is dividend income arising to a spouse, civil partner or minor child from shares that are not an outright gift of ordinary share capital carrying full rights?
factors: Is there an arrangement with an element of bounty (an uncommercial transfer of value)?
Are the shares a separate class (alphabet shares), carry restricted rights, or are dividends waived/varied?
Is the income mainly derived from one person's work in the company?
The s626 exemption for outright gifts between spouses of shares that are not wholly or substantially a right to income
cards.reasoning: The share structure shows features HMRC associates with settlements. No adjustment is computed; the reviewer must assess.

cards.title: Dividend waivers
cards.question: Has a shareholder waived dividends so that others receive more?
factors: Were sufficient reserves available to pay the same rate on all shares without the waiver?
Is the waiver part of a regular pattern?
Does the waiving shareholder's spouse or child benefit?
authorities: Donovan and McLaren v HMRC [2014] UKFTT 048 (TC)
cards.reasoning: A dividend waiver is recorded in the profile.

cards.title: General anti-abuse rule screen
cards.question: Could a planning step be regarded as abusive tax arrangements?
factors: Is obtaining a tax advantage the main purpose, or one of the main purposes?
Is the arrangement a reasonable course of action given the policy of the provisions (double reasonableness)?
Contrived or abnormal steps, or results that Parliament did not anticipate
cards.reasoning: The optimiser only chooses between statutory elections and ordinary remuneration choices. Any scenario that combines a repayment and redraw, circular funds, or dividend waivers is screened here and never recommended.

cards.title: Expenditure on plant and machinery
cards.question: Is the asset plant or machinery used in the business?
cards.notes: Buildings and structures are excluded (s21-22) except items in List C (s23); integral features are plant (s33A).

cards.title: Annual investment allowance
cards.question: How much qualifying expenditure (not cars) should be covered by the AIA?
cards.notes: The limit is time-apportioned for periods other than 12 months (s51A(5)). Cars are excluded (s38B). Claims can be for any amount up to the limit, so a smaller claim is an election.

cards.title: AIA shared between related companies or businesses
cards.question: Is this company related to another (common control and shared premises or similar activities), so one AIA is shared?
factors: Are the businesses controlled by the same person(s)?
The shared premises condition - do they carry on qualifying activities from the same premises?
The similar activities condition - is more than 50% of turnover from the same NACE classification?
Groups of companies share one AIA (s51C) regardless of these conditions
cards.reasoning: An associated company is recorded. The full AIA is provisionally allocated to this company on the assumption that the related business claims none; the reviewer must confirm the allocation.

cards.title: Full expensing (100% first-year allowance)
cards.question: Is the expenditure on new and unused main-rate plant by a company (not a car, not for leasing)?
cards.notes: Companies only. On disposal the whole proceeds are a balancing charge (s45U). Not available for used assets or in the period trade ceases.

cards.title: 50% special rate first-year allowance
cards.question: Is the expenditure on new and unused special rate plant by a company?
cards.notes: The remaining 50% goes into the special rate pool. The AIA (100%) is normally preferred while it is available.

cards.title: 40% first-year allowance for main rate expenditure
cards.question: Is this main-rate expenditure on new and unused plant from 1 January 2026 that does not qualify for full expensing?
authority: CAA 2001 (FYA for main rate expenditure, Finance Act 2026)
cards.notes: Announced at Autumn Budget 2025; extends to unincorporated businesses and assets for leasing. The section number and exact conditions must be confirmed against the enacted Finance Act 2026 - the engine only uses it after the AIA is exhausted, so it rarely binds for SME clients.

cards.title: Cars - pool by CO2 emissions
cards.question: Which pool does the car go into, based on CO2 emissions?
cards.notes: Cars with emissions at or below the threshold go to the main pool; above it to the special rate pool. Cars never get the AIA.

cards.title: Zero-emission cars - 100% first-year allowance
cards.question: Is the car new and unused with zero CO2 emissions (or electrically propelled)?
cards.notes: End date reflects the extension to 31 March 2027 (CT) / 5 April 2027 (IT); confirm.

cards.title: Cars with private use (unincorporated businesses)
cards.question: Is the car or asset used privately by the sole trader?
cards.notes: The asset goes into a single-asset pool; allowances are reduced by the private use proportion. Company assets used privately by directors are taxed as benefits instead.

cards.title: Integral features - special rate expenditure
cards.question: Is the expenditure on an integral feature of a building (electrical, water, heating, lifts, solar shading)?

cards.title: Writing-down allowance - main pool
cards.question: What WDA is due on the main pool?
cards.notes: Reduced proportionately for periods shorter than 12 months (s56(3)). Where the rate changes during a period (1 April 2026 CT / 6 April 2026 IT), a hybrid rate is time-apportioned by days.

cards.title: Writing-down allowance - special rate pool
cards.question: What WDA is due on the special rate pool?

cards.title: Small pools allowance
cards.question: Is the unrelieved balance on the main or special rate pool at or below the small pools limit?
cards.notes: The limit is reduced proportionately for short periods. The engine claims it by default.

cards.title: Disposal value
cards.question: What disposal value is brought into account when an asset leaves a pool?
cards.notes: The lower of proceeds and original cost. A negative pool balance is a balancing charge.

cards.title: Disposal of full-expensed or 50% FYA assets
cards.question: Was the asset disposed of one on which full expensing or the 50% FYA was claimed?
cards.notes: Full expensing - the whole disposal value is an immediate balancing charge. 50% FYA - half is a balancing charge and half reduces the special rate pool.

cards.title: New and unused status not recorded
cards.question: Was the asset new and unused when acquired (needed for full expensing and the 50% FYA)?

cards.title: Structures and buildings allowance
cards.question: Is this qualifying expenditure on constructing, renovating or converting a non-residential structure or building?
cards.notes: Straight line from the later of the date the expenditure was incurred and the date the building was first brought into non-residential use; time-apportioned by days. Land and its acquisition costs are excluded. An allowance statement is required (s270IA).

cards.title: Asset class or pool not determinable
cards.question: What kind of asset is this (plant, car, integral feature, building)?
factors: Function test - is it the apparatus with which the trade is carried on, or the setting in which it is carried on?
List A/B exclusions and List C saving (s21-23)
authorities: Wimpy International Ltd v Warland [1989] STC 273
J Lyons & Co Ltd v A-G [1944] Ch 281
cards.reasoning: Treated as main pool plant pending classification.

cards.title: Trading profits computed on GAAP, adjusted for tax
cards.question: Start from the accounting profit and adjust for items the tax rules treat differently.

cards.title: Accounting periods straddling 31 March

cards.title: Main rate
cards.question: Are augmented profits at or above the upper limit for the period?

cards.title: Small profits rate
cards.question: Are augmented profits at or below the lower limit for the period?
cards.notes: Close investment-holding companies cannot use the small profits rate (CTA 2010 s18N) - flag a CIC in the profile notes.

cards.title: Marginal relief
cards.question: Are augmented profits between the lower and upper limits?
cards.notes: Relief = (U - A) x N/A x standard fraction, where U is the upper limit, A augmented profits and N taxable total profits. Augmented profits include exempt distributions from non-group companies.

cards.title: Limits divided between associated companies
cards.question: How many companies were associated with this company at any time in the accounting period?
cards.notes: Dormant companies and passive holding companies are disregarded (s18E(4)-(5)). The count must be recorded in the client profile; a missing count fails the data health check.

cards.title: Whether companies are associated
cards.question: Does one company control the other, or are both under the control of the same person(s), taking account of attribution of associates' rights?
factors: Direct control (more than 50% of share capital, voting power, income or assets on a winding up)
Rights of associates attributed only where there is substantial commercial interdependence (s18F; CTM03770)
Financial, economic and organisational links between the companies
Whether the other company was dormant or a passive holding company for the whole period
cards.reasoning: The profile records the basis as uncertain. The count in the profile is used provisionally.

cards.title: Limits reduced for short accounting periods
cards.question: Is the accounting period shorter than 12 months?
cards.notes: Engine convention: limits x days in period / 365, rounded to the penny, then allocated to each financial year by days with the remainder in the last slice. A period of 365 or 366 days is a full year (no reduction). Matches the HMRC marginal relief calculator for non-leap periods; check leap-day periods by hand.

cards.title: Trading losses brought forward
cards.question: Are there trading losses carried forward from earlier periods?
cards.notes: Applied against profits of the same trade (s45B) to the extent needed. The deductions allowance (£5m) restriction is not modelled - irrelevant for SME clients below it. Post-April 2017 losses can instead be set against total profits by claim (s45A) - shown as an election.

cards.question: When is the final FPS or EPS for the tax year due?
cards.notes: The final FPS is due on or before the last payday of the year; 19 April is the latest date for an EPS marking the final submission.

cards.title: Ordinary revenue expenses of the trade
cards.question: Is this a routine revenue cost incurred wholly and exclusively for the trade?
cards.notes: Categories are listed only when their ordinary nature is not in doubt. Accountancy fees for preparing accounts and returns are allowable (BIM46450); fees for tax disputes are not, and should be coded to legal_professional with fee_nature=tax_dispute.

cards.title: Director's remuneration
cards.question: Is the director's salary or bonus paid within nine months of the period end?
cards.notes: Accrued remuneration not paid within 9 months of the period end is deductible in the period it is paid.

cards.title: Depreciation and amortisation
cards.question: Is this an accounting charge for depreciation or amortisation of fixed assets?
cards.notes: Capital allowances are given instead. Intangibles under CTA 2009 Part 8 are out of scope for v1.

cards.title: Corporation tax and income tax charged in the accounts
cards.question: Is this a charge for tax on profits?
cards.notes: Tax on profits is an appropriation of profit, as are a sole trader's drawings.

cards.title: Wholly and exclusively (dual purpose)
cards.question: Was the expense incurred wholly and exclusively for the purposes of the trade, or does it have a private purpose too?
cards.notes: Recode the transaction to a specific category where possible.
factors: The object (purpose) of the spender at the time, not the effect of the expense
Whether any private benefit is merely incidental or is itself a purpose
Whether an identifiable business part can be separated (ITTOIA s34(2) / CTA 2009 s54(2))
Evidence: who benefits, how often, link to income-earning activity
authorities: Bentleys, Stokes and Lowless v Beeson [1952] 2 All ER 82
MacKinlay v Arthur Young McClelland Moores & Co [1990] 2 AC 239
Vodafone Cellular Ltd v Shaw [1997] STC 734
cards.reasoning: Sundry costs are uncoded or mixed by nature. Until the purpose is confirmed the prudent default is to disallow; the reviewer can allow in full or allow the separable business part.

cards.title: Mixed-use costs with a recorded business-use percentage
cards.question: What part of this mixed-use cost relates to the business?
cards.notes: Applies where the business-use proportion is recorded on the transaction (e.g. phone, van running costs). Whether the percentage itself is reasonable is for the reviewer when it is first set.

cards.title: Fixed asset additions
cards.question: Is this expenditure on an asset of enduring benefit to the trade?
cards.notes: Excluded from the profit computation and passed to capital allowances via the fixed asset register.

cards.title: Repairs where the nature of the work is not recorded
cards.question: Is this a repair (restoring an asset to its original condition) or an improvement (capital)?
cards.notes: Record improvement=yes/no in the BRG Facts column to resolve automatically.
factors: Is the "entirety" being worked on the whole asset or a subsidiary part of it?
Does the work restore the asset or improve it beyond its original state (like-for-like with modern materials is still a repair)?
Was the asset usable in the trade when acquired, or did the work make it so?
Accounting treatment (capitalised or expensed) is relevant but not decisive
authorities: Law Shipping Co Ltd v CIR (1923) 12 TC 621
Odeon Associated Theatres Ltd v Jones (1971) 48 TC 257
Samuel Jones & Co (Devonvale) Ltd v CIR (1951) 32 TC 513
British Insulated and Helsby Cables Ltd v Atherton [1926] AC 205
cards.reasoning: Coded as repairs in the books; provisionally allowed as revenue pending confirmation that no improvement element exists.

cards.title: Repairs confirmed as like-for-like
cards.question: Is this a repair with no improvement element?

cards.title: Repairs that improve the asset
cards.question: Does the work improve the asset beyond its original condition?
cards.notes: Capital. Add to the fixed asset register if it qualifies for capital allowances or SBA.

cards.title: Entertaining where attendees are not recorded
cards.question: Who was entertained (staff only, or including clients/suppliers)?

cards.title: Business entertainment of non-employees
cards.question: Is this business entertainment of non-employees?
cards.notes: Staff attending to host clients are part of the business entertainment (BIM45034), so the whole cost is disallowed. Overseas customers: input tax may be recoverable (VIT43000) - recode if so.

cards.title: Staff entertainment
cards.question: Is this entertaining of employees only?
cards.notes: Allowable for the employer. For the employees, an annual function costing no more than the staff_function_limit per head is exempt (ITEPA s264); above it the whole cost is a benefit. A sole trader entertaining only themselves is not staff entertaining - code it as drawings.

cards.title: Client gifts carrying a conspicuous advertisement, within the limit
cards.question: Is the gift branded, not food/drink/tobacco/vouchers, and within the per-recipient limit?

cards.title: Other client gifts
cards.question: Is this a gift that falls outside the conspicuous-advertisement exception?
cards.notes: Gifts are business entertainment unless the s1300/s47 exception is met (all conditions recorded). Input tax is recoverable on business gifts, but output tax is due where gifts to the same person exceed the VAT gift limit in 12 months.

cards.title: Trivial benefits to staff
cards.question: Is this a staff gift of no more than the trivial-benefit limit, not cash or a cash voucher, and not a reward for services?
cards.notes: Exempt for the employee. Directors of close companies (and their household) are capped at the annual director cap - the director totals are checked in the extraction module.

cards.title: Staff gifts outside the trivial-benefit exemption
cards.question: Is this a staff gift that is cash, a cash voucher, a reward, or over the limit?
cards.notes: Allowable employment cost for the company, but a taxable benefit for the employee (P11D or PAYE Settlement Agreement).

cards.title: Car lease rentals - high emission cars
cards.question: Is this a lease rental for a car with CO2 emissions above the threshold?
cards.notes: The 15% restriction applies to hire of cars first registered before 1 April 2009 under older rules - not modelled. VAT: 50% of input tax on a car lease is blocked where the car is available for private use; recode with exclusive_business_use=yes for a pool car.

cards.title: Car lease rentals - low emission cars
cards.question: Is this a lease rental for a car at or below the CO2 threshold?

cards.title: Car lease where CO2 is not recorded
cards.question: What are the car's CO2 emissions (g/km)?

cards.title: Mileage claims at approved rates
cards.question: Is the mileage claim within the approved mileage allowance for the business miles recorded?
cards.notes: Company: payments to directors up to the approved amount are deductible and free of tax/NIC; any excess is shown as disallowed here only for the sole-trader simplified-expenses election, and as a taxable payment for a company (deductible, but reported via payroll). Sole trader: the flat rate (s94D) replaces actual motoring costs and capital allowances for that vehicle. VAT on fuel within a mileage allowance is not modelled (needs fuel receipts) - treated as no VAT.

cards.title: Mileage claims with no miles recorded
cards.question: How many business miles does this claim cover?

cards.title: Travel to a temporary workplace
cards.question: Was the journey to a temporary workplace (not ordinary commuting)?

cards.title: Ordinary commuting
cards.question: Is this ordinary commuting between home and a permanent place of business?
cards.notes: For a company the cost of an employee's commuting is deductible as an employment cost but taxable on the employee; the disallowance here applies to sole traders. Recode company commuting costs to wages with a benefit flag.

cards.title: Travel and subsistence where the workplace status is unknown
cards.question: Is the destination a temporary workplace or a permanent base?
factors: Is there a base of operations from which the business is run?
Is attendance at the destination for a limited duration or temporary purpose (24-month rule for employees)?
Are journeys regular and predictable (indicating a permanent place)?
For meals, was the trader away from their normal pattern of business travel?
cards.reasoning: Coded as business travel; provisionally allowed pending confirmation of the destination's status.

cards.title: Use of home - simplified flat rate (sole traders)
cards.question: How many hours a month was the home used for business?
cards.notes: The allowable amount is the flat monthly rate for the band of hours, for each month recorded (months fact, default 12).

cards.title: Use of home - actual cost apportionment
cards.question: What part of the household costs relates to business use, and is that apportionment reasonable?
cards.notes: Flat-rate claims by sole traders with recorded hours are resolved automatically by EXP-HOME-01.
factors: Number of rooms used and whether any room is used exclusively for business (CGT private residence relief risk)
Hours of business use against total use
Which costs are fixed (council tax, mortgage interest, rent) and which vary with use (heat, light)
For a company paying a director - is there a written arrangement and evidence of the additional household costs?
Payments up to the employee flat rate per week are exempt without evidence (ITEPA s316A)
cards.reasoning: The claim is provisionally allowed for the business. For a company, only the employee flat rate per week is exempt for the director without evidence; any excess is at risk of being taxable earnings.

cards.title: Pre-trading expenditure
cards.question: Was this incurred before trading began, and within the pre-trading window?
cards.notes: Allowed as if incurred on the first day of trading if within the window and otherwise deductible; older costs are disallowed. This is an overlay: the category's own rule still decides whether the cost would have been deductible (e.g. entertaining stays disallowed); the window test is applied on top.

cards.title: Fines and penalties of the business
cards.question: Is this a fine or penalty imposed on the business itself?
cards.notes: Penalties for breaking the law are not incurred for the purposes of the trade (McKnight v Sheppard [1999] 1 WLR 1333). Late-payment interest and penalties to HMRC are likewise disallowed (CTA 2009 s1303).

cards.title: Employee's fine paid by the employer
cards.question: Is this a fine incurred by an employee personally that the company has paid?
cards.notes: Deductible as part of the employee's remuneration package, but taxable earnings for the employee (payroll/P11D).

cards.title: Legal and professional fees of a revenue nature
cards.question: Do the fees relate to the day-to-day trade (debt collection, trade contracts, employment matters, short leases)?

cards.title: Legal and professional fees of a capital nature
cards.question: Do the fees relate to acquiring or disposing of a capital asset, a long lease, or share capital?
cards.notes: Capital fees may form part of an asset's cost for capital allowances, SBA or chargeable gains - add to the register where they do.

cards.title: Legal and professional fees - nature not recorded
cards.question: Are these fees revenue (trading) or capital in nature?
factors: What was the fee for - an asset, a lease of more than 50 years, share issue, or the trade's day-to-day operation?
Does it preserve an existing asset or right (revenue) or acquire/enhance one (capital)?
Is any part a tax dispute (disallowed) or a personal matter?
authorities: ECC Quarries Ltd v Watkis [1975] STC 578
Morgan v Tate & Lyle Ltd [1955] AC 21
cards.reasoning: Provisionally allowed as revenue; request the invoice narrative to confirm.

cards.title: Training that updates existing skills
cards.question: Does the training update or maintain skills already used in the trade?

cards.title: Training for a new skill or qualification
cards.question: Does the training give the trader a new skill or qualification (capital / personal)?
cards.notes: For a company, training of employees is generally allowable (and exempt for the employee under ITEPA s250).
factors: Is the course connected to the trade as currently carried on?
Does it create an asset of enduring benefit (a new qualification, new trade)?
Is there a personal benefit beyond the trade?
cards.reasoning: For a sole trader, training with no recorded link to existing skills is treated as capital/personal until confirmed.

cards.title: Training of employees and directors (company)
cards.question: Is this work-related training for an employee or director?

cards.title: Telephone and internet (company contract)
cards.question: Is this a phone or broadband contract in the company's name?
cards.notes: One mobile phone per employee provided under a company contract is exempt (ITEPA s319).

cards.title: Telephone and internet (sole trader)
cards.question: What is the business-use proportion of the phone and internet costs?
cards.notes: A business-only line is fully allowable; for mixed use record private_use_pct and EXP-PRIV-01 applies.

cards.title: Motor running costs
cards.question: Are these running costs of a business vehicle?
cards.notes: Sole traders with private use: record private_use_pct (EXP-PRIV-01). Company cars with private use create a car/fuel benefit for the director (P11D) and may need the VAT fuel scale charge.

cards.title: Charitable donations
cards.question: Is this a donation to a charity?
cards.notes: Not a trading expense. A company deducts qualifying charitable donations from total profits (CTA 2010 s189 - applied in the CT computation); a sole trader claims Gift Aid through the return.

cards.title: Employer pension contributions
cards.question: Is this an employer contribution to a registered pension scheme, paid in the period?
cards.notes: Deductible when paid. Large contributions may be spread (FA 2004 s197). Contributions for a director-shareholder are tested for wholly and exclusively only where the overall package is excessive for the work done (BIM46035) - escalate in the review queue if that is in doubt.

cards.title: Research and development costs
cards.question: Is this a revenue cost of research and development related to the trade?
cards.notes: Deductible as revenue expenditure. Whether R&D relief (RDEC / ERIS) is available is a separate judgment raised once per period by CT-RD-01 and is not computed in v1.

cards.title: Uncategorised transaction
cards.question: What is this transaction? (The nominal code is not in the mapping.)

cards.title: No specific rule for this combination of facts
cards.question: Is this cost deductible on general principles (revenue, wholly and exclusively, not prohibited)?
factors: Revenue or capital in nature?
Incurred wholly and exclusively for the trade?
Any specific statutory prohibition (entertaining, crime-related payments, unpaid remuneration)?
authorities: British Insulated and Helsby Cables Ltd v Atherton [1926] AC 205
cards.reasoning: The category has no specific rule for the facts recorded. Provisionally allowed as booked; the reviewer should confirm or add a rule.

cards.title: Income tax on employment and other non-savings income
cards.question: How much income tax is due on salary and other non-savings income?

cards.title: Scottish rates on non-savings, non-dividend income
cards.question: Is the individual a Scottish taxpayer (main place of residence in Scotland)?
cards.notes: Savings and dividend income are taxed at UK rates using the UK basic rate band.

cards.title: Welsh rates of income tax
cards.question: Is the individual a Welsh taxpayer?

cards.title: Personal allowance taper
cards.question: Does adjusted net income exceed the taper threshold?
cards.notes: The allowance falls by £1 for every £2 of adjusted net income above the threshold. Personal pension contributions and Gift Aid (which reduce adjusted net income) are not modelled.

cards.title: Dividend income tax
cards.question: How much tax is due on dividends after the dividend allowance?
cards.notes: Dividends are the top slice of income. The allowance uses up band - it is a nil rate, not an exemption.

cards.title: Distributable reserves - hard stop
cards.question: Does the dividend exceed profits available for distribution?
cards.notes: A dividend beyond distributable reserves is unlawful; a shareholder who knew or had reasonable grounds to believe it was unlawful must repay it (s847), and HMRC may treat it as a loan (s455) or earnings. The optimiser never proposes it; any scenario that does is marked as a hard stop.

cards.title: Class 1 NIC for directors (annual earnings period)
cards.question: What employee and employer NIC is due on the director's salary?
cards.notes: Directors use an annual earnings period, so the thresholds are applied to the year's total salary.

cards.title: Qualifying year without paying NIC
cards.question: Is salary at or above the lower earnings limit (a qualifying year for state pension)?

cards.title: Employment Allowance
cards.question: Can the company claim the Employment Allowance against employer NIC?
cards.notes: Excluded where the director is the only employee paid above the secondary threshold (SI 2016/344), so a single-director company with no other staff cannot claim. Two directors both paid above the threshold, or another employee above it, restores eligibility. Connected companies share one allowance. The £100,000 prior-year employer NIC limit applied up to 2024-25.

cards.title: Salary level
cards.question: What salary should each director take?
cards.notes: A commercial salary for work done is deductible. The optimiser tests standard points (nil, LEL, ST, PT) and a grid.

cards.title: Employer pension contributions
cards.question: Should the company contribute to the director's pension?
cards.notes: Deductible for CT when paid, no NIC, not taxable on the director within the annual allowance. Carry forward of unused allowance from the three previous years is not modelled - contributions above the current-year allowance are flagged, not blocked.

cards.title: s455 charge on loans to participators
cards.question: Is a loan to a participator in a close company outstanding at the end of the accounting period?
cards.notes: Charged on the amount outstanding at the period end that has not been repaid, released or written off within nine months and one day; due with the corporation tax. The rate is the one in force when the loan was made.

cards.title: s458 relief on repayment
cards.question: Has a loan on which s455 was charged since been repaid?
cards.notes: Relief is due nine months and one day after the end of the accounting period in which the repayment is made; claim within four years.

cards.title: Beneficial loan benefit
cards.question: Did the director's loans exceed the threshold at any time in the tax year at below the official rate of interest?
cards.notes: Normal averaging method by default; Class 1A NIC on the benefit at the secondary rate.

cards.title: Alternative (precise) method for beneficial loans
cards.question: Should the precise (daily balance) method be used instead of normal averaging?
cards.notes: The employee may elect (by the SA filing date) and HMRC may require it. Both figures are shown.

cards.title: Clearing an overdrawn loan account before the s455 date
cards.question: Should the overdrawn balance be cleared (dividend, bonus or cash) before the s455 due date?
cards.notes: Clearing by a declared dividend or bonus is a genuine repayment and is excluded from the bed-and-breakfasting rules (s464C(4)). Clearing by cash that is then redrawn is not - see AA-464C-01.

cards.title: Employment status (IR35 / off-payroll working)
cards.question: Would the director be an employee of the end client if engaged directly (hypothetical contract)?
factors: Mutuality of obligation - an obligation to provide and accept work
Control - over what, how, when and where the work is done
Personal service and genuine right of substitution
Part and parcel of the client's organisation
Financial risk, own equipment, opportunity to profit, multiple clients
Who decides status - client size (small client: the company decides under Chapter 8; medium/large client: the client issues an SDS under Chapter 10)
authorities: Ready Mixed Concrete (South East) Ltd v Minister of Pensions [1968] 2 QB 497
HMRC v Atholl House Productions Ltd [2022] EWCA Civ 501
HMRC v Professional Game Match Officials Ltd [2024] UKSC 29
Christa Ackroyd Media Ltd v HMRC [2019] UKUT 326 (TCC)
Kickabout Productions Ltd v HMRC [2022] EWCA Civ 502
cards.reasoning: No status determination is on file. No deemed employment payment is included in the computation; the review item shows the estimated Chapter 8 deemed payment and tax if the engagement is inside.

cards.title: Trivial benefits cap for directors of close companies
cards.question: Do trivial benefits to a director (and household) exceed the annual cap?

cards.title: Trading income
cards.question: Is this a receipt of the trade?
cards.notes: Output tax on sales is tested in the VAT module, not here.

cards.title: Interest received by a company
cards.question: Is this interest from a loan relationship (e.g. a bank deposit)?
cards.notes: A non-trading loan relationship credit - part of total profits but not trading profits.

cards.title: Interest received by a sole trader
cards.question: Is this savings interest rather than trading income?
cards.notes: Excluded from trading profits; savings income is outside the v1 income tax computation and is flagged.

cards.title: Trading profits of an unincorporated business
cards.question: Start from the accounting profit and adjust for tax.

cards.title: Tax year basis of assessment
cards.question: Which profits are taxed in the tax year?
cards.notes: From 2024-25 the profits of the tax year are taxed, apportioned by days from overlapping accounting periods. An accounting date of 31 March to 4 April is treated as 5 April (s209A - section reference to be confirmed). Non-aligned year ends need the next period's figures or an estimate.

cards.title: 2023-24 transition year
cards.question: Does the business have a non-aligned accounting date for 2023-24, giving transition profit and overlap relief?
factors: Accounting date - aligned (31 March to 5 April) businesses have no transition profit
Overlap profit brought forward from commencement
Transition profit spread over five years unless an election accelerates it
cards.reasoning: Transition profits are not computed in v1. Provide overlap profit figures to review by hand.

cards.title: Income tax on self-employment profits
cards.question: What income tax is due on the year's profits and other income?

cards.title: Class 4 NIC
cards.question: What Class 4 NIC is due on profits between the limits?

cards.title: Class 2 NIC status
cards.question: Is Class 2 payable, credited, or voluntary for the year?
cards.notes: 2023-24: payable on profits at or above the lower profits limit; credited between the small profits threshold and that limit. From 2024-25: nothing payable; credited at or above the threshold; voluntary below it (the engine shows the voluntary cost as an option, not a liability).

cards.title: Payments on account
cards.question: Are payments on account due for the next year?
cards.notes: Each payment is half the year's income tax and Class 4 (not Class 2 or CGT), unless the liability is below the threshold or 80%+ was deducted at source.

cards.title: Reducing payments on account
cards.question: Should payments on account be reduced because the next year's liability is expected to be lower?
cards.notes: Interest is charged if the reduction proves excessive.

cards.title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
cards.question: Is qualifying income (gross self-employment and property income) for the reference year above the threshold?
guidance: GOV.UK MTD for Income Tax eligibility
cards.notes: Qualifying income is turnover, not profit. Mandation starts in the tax year shown in the schedule, based on the return for the reference year two years earlier.

cards.title: Simplified expenses
cards.question: Should flat-rate vehicle and use-of-home amounts be used instead of actual costs?

cards.title: Trading allowance
cards.question: Should the trading allowance be deducted instead of actual expenses?

cards.title: Is there a trade?
cards.question: Is the activity a trade (rather than a hobby, investment or one-off)?
factors: Profit-seeking motive
Number and frequency of transactions
Modification of assets to make them more saleable
Nature of the asset, manner of acquisition, interval between purchase and sale
Existence of similar trading transactions, and the method of finance
authorities: Royal Commission on the Taxation of Profits and Income (1955) - badges of trade
cards.reasoning: The profile records trading status as uncertain; computed as a trade pending review.

cards.title: Sole trader vs limited company comparison
cards.question: At this profit level, how do total tax and net income compare if the business is run through a company?
cards.notes: Illustrative only. Excludes incorporation costs, CGT on goodwill (incorporation relief s162 or s162A election), restrictions on relief for goodwill acquired from related individuals (CTA 2009 s849B), stamp duty, and the extra admin cost (taken from policy.json). Not a recommendation to incorporate.

cards.title: Business not registered for VAT
cards.question: Is the business registered for VAT on the transaction date?
cards.notes: VAT paid is part of the cost (and allowable or capital with it). Pre-registration input tax (SI 1995/2518 reg 111) is not modelled.

cards.title: Input tax on taxable business purchases
cards.question: Is VAT charged on a purchase used for making taxable supplies?
cards.notes: Assumes wholly taxable supplies. Businesses with exempt supplies are flagged for partial exemption (VAT-PE-01).

cards.title: No VAT on the purchase
cards.question: Is the purchase zero-rated, exempt or outside the scope of VAT?

cards.title: Business entertainment - input tax blocked
cards.question: Is this business entertainment of non-employees?

cards.title: Purchase of a car - input tax blocked
cards.question: Is this the purchase of a motor car (as defined) that is available for private use?
cards.notes: Recoverable only where the car is used exclusively for business with no availability for private use (e.g. a pool car), or for a taxi/driving school/leasing trade.

cards.title: Purchase of a car used exclusively for business
cards.question: Is the car used exclusively for business, with no private availability?

cards.title: Road fuel with private use
cards.question: Is fuel bought for a vehicle that is also used privately?

cards.title: Compulsory registration - historic turnover test
cards.question: Did taxable turnover in the last 12 months exceed the registration threshold at the end of any month?
cards.notes: Notify HMRC within 30 days of the end of the month in which the threshold was exceeded; registration takes effect from the first day of the second month. The exception where turnover in the next 12 months is not expected to exceed the deregistration threshold (para 1(3)) is shown but not auto-applied.

cards.title: Compulsory registration - forward-look test
cards.question: Is taxable turnover in the next 30 days alone expected to exceed the registration threshold?
cards.notes: Registration is from the start of the 30-day period; notify by the end of it.

cards.title: Voluntary deregistration
cards.question: Is taxable turnover in the next 12 months expected to be at or below the deregistration threshold?
cards.notes: Output tax is due on stock and assets held at deregistration (VATA Sch 4 para 8) if it exceeds £1,000.

cards.title: Flat rate scheme - eligibility and comparison
cards.question: Is the business eligible for the flat rate scheme, and would it pay less VAT?
cards.notes: Sector selection is the business's main activity by turnover; a disputed sector should be resolved before joining.

cards.title: Flat rate scheme - limited cost trader test
cards.question: Is the business's spend on relevant goods less than 2% of VAT-inclusive turnover or below the annual minimum?
cards.notes: Relevant goods exclude capital items, food and drink for staff, vehicle costs including fuel (unless a transport business) and goods for resale or hire unless that is the main business. The engine counts transactions with relevant_goods=yes, or categories cost_of_sales/materials by default.

cards.title: Cash accounting scheme eligibility
cards.question: Is estimated taxable turnover in the next 12 months within the cash accounting limit?

cards.title: Annual accounting scheme eligibility
cards.question: Is estimated taxable turnover in the next 12 months within the annual accounting limit?

cards.title: Partial exemption (out of scope for v1)
cards.question: Does the business make exempt supplies, so input tax must be apportioned?
factors: Value of exempt supplies and directly attributable exempt input tax
De minimis tests (simplified tests 1 and 2, standard test)
Whether a special method is in place
authorities: Commissioners of Customs and Excise v Midland Bank plc (C-98/98) [2000] STC 501
cards.reasoning: Input tax has been treated as fully recoverable. Partial exemption is not computed in v1; this must be worked by hand.
